thread:
incident-bot: PAGING: GPU_POOL_EXHAUSTED in eu-west3 — autoscaler stalled, queue growth > 600s (alerts: gpu_pool_saturation, autoscaler_stall)
alex: got the alert. I'm oncall. Confirming impact: internal autoscaler shows pending pods awaiting GPUs, region quotas at limit.
maria: on it — can you post the runbook link? I have some customers seeing increased 429s.
alex: runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/gpu-quota-exhaustion
sophie: seeing backlog on inference-rt: write_q_len=1200, avg_wait=8.2s, token_throttle_events=112 in last 10m.
jamie: @alex any automatic fallback to lower-GPU or CPU-only variants configured?
alex: we have model-fallback policy but it's per-deployment and many customers pinned to dedicated GPU variants. Fallback attempted but failed due to region affinity rule.
infra-bot: autoscaler: ScaleUpRequest(region=eu-west3, requested_gpus=48) => ProvisionDenied(quota_exceeded)
alex: timeline: scale request at 2157779940, denied immediately. Autoscaler retried 3x and then paused.
maria: customer-support: several PAYG customers report 429 on hosted API; high traffic from a single enterprise test tenant amplified queue. CS escalating.
jamie: can we move some non-critical workloads to another region? e.g., eu-west1 or us-central1?
sophie: risk: many models are pinned and customer data locality prevents cross-region routing for some private deployments. But hosted API traffic could be routed.
alex: mitigation plan (short): 1) throttle heavy tenant via per-API-key rate-limit 2) enable CPU fallback for public-hosted routes 3) request quota bump from GCP 4) open cross-region fallback for eligible workloads.
alex: doing step 1 now: throttling the offending API key by 60%.
deploy-bot: Applied rate limit config: /services/api/keys/ak_live_47 -> rate_limit=40rps (was unlimited)
maria: step 1 applied. I'm seeing immediate reduction in queue growth, backlog down to 820 -> 620 in 3m.
alex: step 2: enabling cpu-fallback on route group hosted-text-gen-v2. Will toggle canary first.
deploy-bot: Canary enable: hosted-text-gen-v2 -> cpu_fallback=true (10% traffic)
jamie: logs from the canary: fallback success rate 95%, latency up ~300ms but no throttles.
sophie: can we increase canary to 50%? need safety check.
alex: increasing to 50% to relieve GPU pressure.
deploy-bot: Update: hosted-text-gen-v2 -> cpu_fallback=50%
infra-bot: observed effect: gpu_pending_pods=210 -> 120 within 6 minutes. Node GPU utilization at 98% still, but queue median_wait down to 2.1s.
alex: filing quota request with GCP support and adding priority escalation. Contacting rep.
alex: support case created: https://console.cloud.google.com/support/cases/CASE-90817 — asking for temporary quota increase + explanation of sudden spike.
maria: customer-support: notifying affected customers in batches. Short note: "We're mitigating by routing traffic to CPU fallback and applying temporary rate limits; expected improvement in next 20 minutes."
customer-support: posted update to customers: https://support.redwood/status/2157779999
jamie: what about Dedicated pools? any failovers possible from dedicated to shared-hosted?
sophie: dedicated pools are isolated. Some teams have burst-to-hosted enabled; we should check which customers allowed that.
alex: running query to list eligible deployments for burst-to-hosted.
alex: found 7 eligible deployments, 4 opted in. Initiating manual burst for the largest one.
alex: manual burst triggered for dep=dp-843 -> shifted 12 GPUs worth of workload to hosted_pools.
infra-bot: Burst action accepted: moved 3 jobs to hosted nodes. This will clear ~20% of pending GPU requests.
maria: monitoring impact — queue down to 320, error rates trending down for hosted customers.
sophie: we should still prepare for the scenario GCP denies quota bump. Plan B: extend CPU fallback to 90% and enforce stricter tenant-level throttles.
jamie: can we deploy lightweight model-quantized variants to reduce GPU per-request cost? That'd buy more headroom.
alex: good idea. but build+deploy time ~25-40m. We'll prioritize traffic shaping first.
alex: Escalation: paging cloud team lead to confirm quota path and potential emergency lift.
alex: @oncall-cloud? (note: cloud lead out-of-hours might take longer; we've marked case as P1)
incident-bot: PagerDuty: Incident 11245 -> escalated to cloud-team-lead
jamie: while we wait, can support prepare refund/cx comms if degradation persists? customer-support: can you prepare churn-sensitive messaging?
customer-support: drafting notice and refund options.
maria: update: GCP says they can review but need 30-90m for temporary quota increase. They asked for traffic pattern and justification.
alex: uploaded traffic snapshot and mitigation steps to case.
alex: while GCP evaluates, let's start extending CPU fallback to 80% for all eligible hosted routes.
deploy-bot: Rolling update: hosted-text-gen-v2 -> cpu_fallback=80% (progress 30/80)
sophie: Early numbers: queue down to 120, pending_gpus=32, token_throttle_events nearly zero.
alex: GCP responded: can grant +24 GPUs temporarily in eu-west3 for 90 minutes. Approving.
alex: applying granted quota increase at cloud console and notifying autoscaler.
infra-bot: Quota updated: eu-west3.gpu_count increased by 24 (temporary)
infra-bot: Autoscaler: re-evaluating pending requests => ScaleUpRequest(requested_gpus=28) => ProvisionAccepted
alex: autoscaler provisioning started; expected nodes coming up in ~6 minutes.
maria: customer-support: posting follow-up: "We're seeing improvements; traffic being routed to fallbacks; expected to resolve in <20m."
jamie: once nodes come up, we should gradually remove CPU fallback to return to baseline.
alex: agreed. plan to ramp CPU fallback down after stable node join and backlog cleared.
sophie: note for postmortem: consider automated cross-region fallback for non-data-local workloads, and pre-approved emergency quota playbook.
alex: agreed. capturing action items in incident doc.
incident-bot: Incident 11245 status -> mitigated. Root cause: regional GPU quota exhausted by traffic spike + pinned deployments prevented automatic cross-region failover. Next steps: runbook updates, quota pre-approvals, improved tenant throttling heuristics.
alex: closing the pager. final checks: queue=0, pending_gpus=0, error_rate at baseline.
maria: creating postmortem draft and customer impact summary.
customer-support: posting final customer update and apology; offering credits to top affected.
jamie: thanks all — good coordination.
sophie: filing follow up tickets: RT-3421 (cross-region fallback), RT-3422 (quota playbook), RT-3423 (tenant throttling automation)
alex: thanks team. I'll update oncall notes and mark this resolved.
